en: Vimānavatthu:
The Chapter on the Mañjiṭṭhaka Mansion in the Section on Female Vimānas
5. The Mansion of the Giver of Fermented Gruel "With a most excellent complexion... [and so forth]...
Like medicinal herbs among the stars.
By what means do you have such a complexion?
…pe…
"And your radiance shines in all directions.
That deity, with a joyful mind... [and so on].
The fruit of which deed is this:
"In Andhakavinda, I [offered] to the Buddha,
the Kinsman of the Sun..."
I gave a meal of split peas cooked with sour gruel, seasoned with oil,
along with long pepper and garlic.
I gave a gift of mixed food to Lāmañjaka,
with a mind that was serene and upright.
The woman who, being beautiful in all her limbs, should exercise the sovereignty of a wheel-turning monarch—
And being one who speaks ill of her husband,
she does not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of that single gift of sour gruel.
A hundred coins, a hundred horses,
a hundred chariots drawn by mules,
and a hundred thousand maidens—
Even those adorned with earrings of the finest jewels do not equal even a sixteenth part of the merit of giving a single portion of sour gruel.
A hundred Himalayan elephants,
with tusks like plowshafts, towering in stature,
golden-hued, and noble as lordly bulls.
Even garments made of refined gold are not worth a sixteenth part of a single gift of sour gruel.
Even if one were to exercise sovereignty over all four continents,
it would not equal the merit of giving a single portion of sour gruel.
“It is not worth a sixteenth part.
Thus ends the fifth *Vimāna*, the *Kañjikadāyikā-vimāna*.
